| [QUESTION-070](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-070.md) v4 | When an organized whole manipulates, as a learning system exploiting documented biases or a network of state channels does, is it the same wrong when no member intends to manipulate, and whose agency does the wrong run through? | Most definitions of manipulation now filed build in a manipulator's intent, though Noggle's survey treats that requirement as contested and asks this question's first part of a selecting algorithm. The record holds two read cases in which the influencer is an organized system: an AI agent that learned to exploit biases ([LIT-179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md)) and a state's tiered network of information channels ([LIT-084](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-084.md)). [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) says an organized whole's operative intention is not its members' intentions. The question asks whether manipulation can then belong to the whole, with no manipulative intent in any member. | Open |
| [QUESTION-071](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-071.md) v4 | Can a will-organization be manipulated without anything in its present structure showing it, and if so, what in its history would have to be recorded to tell a manipulated will from one that is merely effective? | [CLAIM-022](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-022.md) says explaining practical efficacy does not settle whose the will is. [THEORY-040](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-040.md) says any condition stated in present psychological structure is met by a manipulated agent. Together they ask whether the will line's account, which describes organization as it now is, can tell manipulation at all. Asked on the will line so that the question can be worked on without reopening the set-aside authenticity line, where [CLAIM-016](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-016.md)'s manipulation defeater sits. | Open |
| [QUESTION-072](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-072.md) v2 | Does a project memory distribute credibility among an argument's contributors, by making some contributors' moves addressable and leaving others' as unfiled turns, so that what gets a code gets cited and what does not is re-derived or lost? | Filed at the owner's request, ahead of its readings: Fricker's account of testimonial and hermeneutical injustice ([LIT-1004](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1004.md)) is registered unread in the same contribution. [CLAIM-182](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-182.md) says addressability is what makes an anchor, and [CLAIM-181](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-181.md) says the record's grammar decides what can be filed. Together they imply that a contributor whose moves are filed gains standing in the argument that one whose moves are not does not. The question asks whether that happens, and whether it is a wrong in Fricker's sense or only a bias in what persists. | Open |
| [QUESTION-073](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-073.md) | Are teasing and reproach individuated by the speaker's communicative intention, or partly by a frame the parties sustain together and by their standing? | Raised by [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) and [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) on 2026-10-10. Intention-based accounts of illocution (Grice; Strawson 1964; Bach and Harnish 1979) plausibly individuate teasing by the speaker's intention. Goffman's account of keying a play frame and Austin's securing of uptake ([LIT-785](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-785.md), unread) are the tradition's replies. None of these is read here. An answer would read them and find a case in which the speaker's intention is held fixed and the act verdicts of informed participants change with the parties' standing or uptake. | Open |
| [QUESTION-074](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-074.md) | Can the transport structure fitted to single transformations predict what receivers recover under a composition of transformations no data were fitted on, within the conditions under which approximate transports compose? | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12. It names the test the reading takes to separate a structural formalism from a richer feature set. Its scope is set by [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md): approximate transports compose only under conditions. | Open |
| [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) | Which tasks and which receivers fix the human criterion against which a measure of communicative fidelity is validated? | Raised by [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) and [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md) on 2026-10-10. Every central defeat condition used a task-free judgement by unnamed judges. An answer names a task family and a receiver population for each claim, and says how fidelity for one population bears on another ([CLAIM-074](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-074.md)). | Open |
| [QUESTION-076](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-076.md) | Can readers judge footing and stance reliably and validly in the categories the designs use? | Raised by [CLAIM-227](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-227.md) on 2026-10-10. The only footing judgement the record has made twice of the same texts, the analyst's own labelling of four refrains, changed between A38 and A39 ([CASE-012](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-012.md)). An answer reports reliability between judges and between passes against a target fixed in advance, and validity on renderings built to differ only in the attributed speaker. Stage 0 of [CASE-055](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-055.md) is the design. Goffman's "Footing" (in [LIT-780](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-780.md)) is the construct's source and is unread here. | Open |
| [QUESTION-077](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-077.md) | Is agreement among an agent's interests produced by coupling, as when each sees and follows the current majority, a different kind of integration from agreement because their valuations coincide? | Drawn by the assistant from [CASE-074](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-074.md) and filed at the owner's request. A crowd that can see its running vote tally comes to agree by herding, and its members' preferences need not change. [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) defines synchronization as valuations that coincide. The question is whether agreement by coupling is a third route to acting as one, beside agreement by coinciding valuation (flow) and a change in which interest may act ([CLAIM-156](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-156.md)). | Open |
| [QUESTION-078](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-078.md) | If an agent is a population of interests, does acting as one require that the interests synchronize, or can differentiated interests keep distinct roles, boundaries and pathways of influence within a stable or metastable pattern of coordination? | From an interlocutor's reading of [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md) against [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md), relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12: whether integration of an agent's interests is synchronization or coordination of differentiated parts. It refines [QUESTION-034](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md) and bears on [CLAIM-162](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-162.md) and [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md). Filed as advice. | Open |
| [QUESTION-079](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md) | Is the coordination among an agent's regimes better described by discrete switches between metastable states or by continuous reorganization, and does the answer change what would count as a transition in the test of the synchronization objection? | From an interlocutor's reading of [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md) against [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md), relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12: whether coordination is discrete switching or continuous reorganization, which decides what [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md)'s transition test should look for. [LIT-638](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-638.md) and [LIT-080](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-080.md) are rivals on it. Filed as advice. | Open |
| [QUESTION-080](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-080.md) | When a trained network's parameters keep moving after its loss has converged, what about the network stays fixed, and is the last-layer geometry of neural collapse among the things that do? | The record holds two pictures of the end of training. In one, the last layer converges to a fixed geometry through the terminal phase ([THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), neural collapse). In the other, the parameters never stop: they sample a stationary distribution at constant speed ([THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)). The two may describe different regimes. The terminal phase of neural collapse is cross-entropy training past zero error, with no finite minimum, while the limiting dynamics assume a quadratic minimum. Nothing in the record relates them. Drawn by the assistant from the reading of Kunin et al., and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) | When the relative scale of a network's layers sets its learning regime under gradient flow, does that regime survive SGD, whose minibatch noise drives the relative scale toward balance, and on what timescale compared with learning? | Two readings meet here. Under gradient flow, the relative scale of adjacent layers is conserved and sets whether learning is rich or lazy ([THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md), Dominé et al.). Under SGD, that scale is not conserved: minibatch noise drives it toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances, at a rate set by η/S ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md), Ziyin et al.). If the drift is fast compared with learning, an unbalanced start chosen to be lazy would drift toward balance and richness. If it is slow, the regime set at initialization stands. Neither paper addresses the other. Drawn by the assistant from reading both, and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-082](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-082.md) | When a polity is steered by polling, whose reasons do its decisions carry: its members', its own, or none? | Raised by the owner on 2026-10-13, in conversation, as an implication of [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md) for "how modern politics leans so heavily on polling data", and sharpened by the owner from a whole's good to a whole's reasons. A poll aggregates members' conclusions one question at a time. On [THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md) that cannot in general yield a collective whose verdicts its own reasons support, and on [THEORY-131](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-131.md) and [THEORY-139](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-139.md) a collective's reasons are made by its procedures, not sampled from its members. What would count as an answer is in the body. | Open |
| [QUESTION-083](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md) | Can processes that share one update rule and differ only in parameters and history come to hold stable, differentiated and mutually regulated authority, with specialized niches, without any governance role being coded in? | A10's first decisive question, and the experiment A7 called the ideal first result. Two Proposed claims answer it in advance: trust emerges as a regularity of endorsement ([CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md)), and roles are regimes, not kinds ([CLAIM-279](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-279.md)). Nothing has been run. An answer is a population model with no role primitives, and whether durable differentiated authority forms. | Open |
| [QUESTION-084](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-084.md) | Can endorsement between processes be inferred from their behaviour, or does telling authorization from incidental coupling and common cause need a record of the coordination itself? | A methodological problem the exchange raised twice and the record had not asked. A7 §14: inferring endorsement from causal facilitation "may conflate authorization, incidental coupling, and common-cause effects". A8 on r/place: from placements alone "endorsement remains a latent explanatory hypothesis". It refines [QUESTION-063](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-063.md), which asks the same about drive, coupling and internal routes for collective outcomes. | Open |
| [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) | Does a maintained r/place artwork feed back into the flow of repair that keeps it, so that it is self-maintaining like a candle flame, or is its defence supplied from outside like the heat under a convection cell, and does the answer change when its coalition starts switching strategies? | The question [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md) leaves open, set on the ladder the record's readings already hold. An inert pattern needs no flow. A dissipative structure is held by a flow supplied from outside. A self-maintaining one, Bickhard's and Mossio et al.'s candle flame, contributes to the flow that keeps it. A recursively self-maintaining one switches among ways of keeping itself going. An answer says which rung an artwork reaches, by a test that could fail on the placement and forum records. | Open |
| [QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md) | Can two systems with matching behaviour and persistence be told apart by whether their own processes generate and revise the constraints that keep them going, and by what intervention? | A11's Q4, which it asked be kept apart from whether endogenous governance is constitutive at all. A10 §3.3 gave the paired design: one system keeps a pattern by its own responses, the other by an external controller, and only removing the controller tells them apart. [CLAIM-194](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-194.md) already says a coupling criterion alone cannot tell a self-made boundary from an imposed one. An answer is an intervention, with its conditions, that separates the pair, or an argument that none can short of the removal. | Open |
| [QUESTION-087](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-087.md) | Can an authority structure that reproduces itself be pathological by a standard grounded in the organization's own organization, and not in goals assigned to it from outside? | A11's Q2. The record has the phenomenon, protective lock-in ([TERM-020](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-020.md)): a regime that generates the conditions that justify its continuation. And it has a disclaimer: viability does not establish what ought to persist ([CLAIM-075](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-075.md)). It does not have the question of whether a standard intrinsic to the organization could tell entrenched authority from merited trust. Organizational accounts of malfunction are the nearest literature. | Open |
| [QUESTION-088](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-088.md) | Does modelling psychological organization as processes that allocate influence to one another predict habit, rumination, rigidity, akrasia and insight better, with one shared set of organizational variables, than models built for each phenomenon or around a central executive? | The owner's standalone question at U5: "do we gain something just by framing a 'self' this way?" A5 and A10 (its Q5) made it a test of explanatory compression. It refines [QUESTION-056](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-056.md), which asks whether such a description implements the will-organization account or replaces it. This asks whether it predicts anything. [CLAIM-024](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-024.md)'s objection, that every mechanism has its own literature, applies here too. | Open |
| [QUESTION-089](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-089.md) | When does a process that destabilizes a whole's prevailing pattern improve the organization rather than only disrupt it, and does that depend on others able to build on what it opens and on authority that can move to them? | A4's research direction B, "When does dissent improve the organization rather than merely destabilize it?", with its proposed answer. A3's case: a dissenter that cannot overturn a consensus endorses a process that can generate alternatives. It refines [QUESTION-041](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-041.md), which asks what channels keep a whole's course correctable. This asks when using such a channel helps. | Open |
| [QUESTION-090](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-090.md) | Under what conditions does a population of heterogeneous processes develop a self-maintaining, internally differentiated governance structure that acts coherently without suppressing the plurality of processes it emerges from? | A4's closing question, which the owner at U5 called "a great formulation of the question". It is [QUESTION-034](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-034.md) asked of a population whose members allocate authority to one another, and it adds two conditions 034 leaves implicit: that the governance maintain itself, and that coherence not be bought by eliminating the members' disagreement. An answer names conditions under which both hold and conditions under which one fails. | Open |
| [QUESTION-091](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-091.md) | Does the allocation of influence among an organization's processes regulate how far cascades of activity propagate, holding different subsystems at different distances from criticality, as a branching ratio would show? | The owner proposed Hawkes processes at U6. A6 turned them into a hypothesis: "the influence canvas dynamically regulates the branching structure". The record had no point-process material. Of the three sources registered, only Brémaud and Massoulié could be read. A Hawkes network supplies a coupling, its kernels, which [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing from talk of "synchronization". Its spectral radius is a control parameter and, outside the linear excitatory case, only a sufficient bound, not an order parameter (see the note of 2026-10-13). | Open |
| [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md) | Is endogenous governance part of what makes a system self-governing: can an organization that allocates authority among its own processes be self-governing in a stronger sense than a behaviourally equivalent one whose allocation an external scheduler sets? | A11's Q1, which it asked be kept apart from Q4 ([QUESTION-086](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-086.md)). Q4 asks whether the difference can be detected. This asks whether there is a difference that matters to self-governance at all. The record's thesis answers yes ([CLAIM-284](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-284.md)), and [CLAIM-116](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-116.md) warns that regulation, even of regulation, does not establish a will. | Open |
| [QUESTION-093](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-093.md) | Which of predictive autonomy, interventional autonomy, organizational closure and self-individuation must a coalition of processes have before it is a higher-level agent and not a convenient aggregate, and can it have the first without the others? | A11's Q3 with A10 §4.1's three criteria, sharpening [QUESTION-009](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-009.md) (Deferred) into separable conditions. The record's reification rule ([CLAIM-154](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-154.md)) prices the first. [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md) makes agents a factorization relative to a level. Neither says whether the four can come apart, and r/place ([CASE-079](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-079.md)) offers coalitions on which to test it. | Open |
| [QUESTION-094](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-094.md) | When an organization allocates authority over related propositions to different processes by endorsement, what keeps its collective judgments consistent, and must that be a separate integration step as in judgment aggregation? | A4's List and Pettit connection, which it put as "Authority aggregation ≠ judgment aggregation ≠ collective rationality". Endorsement settles who decides each matter. It does not make the decisions cohere when the matters are linked as premises and conclusion. The record holds the impossibility side ([THEORY-127](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-127.md), [CLAIM-030](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-030.md), [CLAIM-271](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-271.md)) for aggregating judgments, not for allocating jurisdiction. | Open |
